01 · About me

About me

I'm a data engineer who believes a pipeline is only finished when the numbers at the end can be trusted. That means validated on the way in, reconciled on the way out, and rerunnable when something goes wrong.

At Cognizant, working for ICICI ERGO General Insurance, I built and maintained an Azure platform for customer, policy, claims, premium and payment data. It used parameterised ADF pipelines, watermark-based incremental loads, Databricks PySpark notebooks and a Bronze → Silver → Gold lakehouse on Delta Lake.

Before that, at Honeywell, I learned the foundations: relational modelling, SQL transformations, load-tracking control tables, and source-to-target reconciliation on every run.

I've since completed an MSc in Data Science in the UK and certified in Microsoft Fabric and Azure Databricks. I'm now looking for my next data engineering role in the UK.

Microsoft Certified: Fabric Data Engineer · Azure Databricks Data Engineer · Azure Fundamentals

Seasons

SEASON 03Jun 2023 – Aug 20263 yrs 3 mos

Associate – Data Engineering

Cognizant · Client: ICICI ERGO General Insurance · Hyderabad, India

Policy and Claims Data Processing Platform. I developed and maintained an Azure platform that ingests and processes customer, policy, claims, premium and payment data. ADF handled ingestion and orchestration, ADLS Gen2 was the storage layer, Databricks did the cleansing and transformation, and a Medallion architecture organised raw, validated and curated data for downstream reporting.

Ingestion & orchestration

  • Built ADF pipelines that ingest CSV and JSON files into ADLS Gen2, using Copy Activity, linked services and reusable datasets.
  • Designed a parameterised, metadata-driven framework: Lookup reads the processing metadata and ForEach loops over each configured dataset through shared pipeline logic.
  • Parameterised source locations, file names, folder paths and destinations, and used dynamic expressions to build storage paths and pass runtime parameters.
  • Used Get Metadata, Switch and If Condition to check source files and route each dataset to the right workflow.
  • Built master orchestration pipelines that coordinate ingestion, validation, transformation and dependent workflows.

Incremental loading

  • Built watermark-based incremental loads: control tables hold the last successful load timestamp, so each run picks up only new records.
  • Updated watermarks only after a successful run, so processing checkpoints stayed reliable and reruns were safe.
  • Applied incremental changes with Delta Lake MERGE and UPDATE to keep target records current.

Transformation & lakehouse

  • Wrote Databricks notebooks in Python, PySpark DataFrames and Spark SQL to cleanse and transform insurance datasets.
  • Handled nulls, removed duplicates, converted data types, and applied filtering, joins and aggregations.
  • Implemented Bronze, Silver and Gold layers to separate raw ingestion, validated data and business-ready datasets.

Quality, monitoring & DevOps

  • Built pre-ingestion checks for file availability, size, expected headers and structural consistency.
  • Implemented error routing and archiving for invalid files, failed runs and successfully ingested files.
  • Ran data quality checks and source-to-target reconciliation to catch missing, duplicate and inconsistent records.
  • Captured pipeline run IDs, status and results for monitoring. Investigated failures and supported controlled reruns.
  • Supported source control and deployments with Git, Azure DevOps and ARM templates.

Business problem

A music-streaming business keeps users, artists, tracks, dates and stream events in an operational Azure SQL database. Analysts needed a governed lakehouse that loads only changed data, keeps dimension history, and can be redeployed safely from dev to prod.

Key engineering decisions
  • 01CDC-based incremental ingestion. Each table's change column is compared with a watermark kept in the lake. Only new rows land in Bronze as Parquet, and then the watermark moves forward.
  • 02Backfill without code changes. An optional from_date per table reloads history on demand, and runs with no new data are detected and skipped.
  • 03Streaming Silver with Auto Loader and Unity Catalog governance. Reusable PySpark utilities, plus Jinja2-templated SQL generated from metadata.
  • 04Gold star schema in Delta Live Tables with SCD Type 2 and data-quality expectations, deployed through Databricks Asset Bundles with Logic Apps failure alerts.

Bank Loan Report Analysis

MSC DISSERTATION · 2025
Dissertation · Computer vision

Waste Classification with Deep Learning

Python · YOLOv8 · PyTorch · Ultralytics · OpenCV · Gradio
Main goal
Automatically sort photos of waste into 8 categories (cardboard, e-waste, food, glass, medical, metal, paper and plastic) with a model light enough for real-time use. The aim is to support smarter recycling and the safe handling of medical and electronic waste.
Method
Explored the TrashBox dataset of about 4,450 images, checking class balance, resolutions, aspect ratios, file formats and colour channels, and cleaned out corrupt and GIF files. Applied augmentation (flips, rotation, shifts, zoom), then fine-tuned a pretrained YOLOv8n-cls model (1.45M parameters) at 224px for 50 epochs with Adam on a Tesla T4 GPU. Built a Gradio app where you upload a photo and get the top 3 predictions.
Result
82.5% top-1 and 97.4% top-5 accuracy on 2,246 validation images, at about 0.4 ms inference per image.

MSC · COMPUTER VISION · JAN 2025
Computer vision · Deep learning

Vehicle Speed Detection in Adverse Weather

Python · YOLOv11 · ByteTrack · OpenCV · Supervision · Gradio
Main goal
Detect and track vehicles in real time from ordinary traffic video, and estimate each vehicle's speed in km/h, accurately, even in rain and fog, where radar, LIDAR and traditional vision methods struggle.
Method
YOLOv11 detects vehicles frame by frame and ByteTrack keeps a consistent ID for each one. A perspective transformation maps pixels to real-world distances, so speed is calculated from how far each vehicle moves over time. Training used weather-augmented data to simulate rain and fog, and a Gradio web app lets users upload a video and get back an annotated one.
Result
Reported detection accuracy of 98% in clear conditions, 94% in rain and 88% in fog, with speed error of about ±2 / ±3 / ±5 km/h. YOLOv11 outperformed YOLOv8 in adverse weather.
